To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a novel mutation in MMP20 that is responsible for hypomaturation AI in one family, and that this mutation is predicted to cause a complete loss of function of MMP20.

a novel mutation was identified in the MMP20 gene in a Turkish family segregating autosomally recessive hypomatration amelogenesis imperfecta and that this mutation abolished the proteolytic activity of MMP20.

a novel mutation (g. 16250T>A; p.H226Q) was identified in the MMP20 gene, which resulted in loss of proteolytic activity in a Turkish family with autosomal recessively inherited hypomaturation AI, and that the MMP20 gene was screened in 14 additional Turkish families, and no additional MMP20 mutations were identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel MMP20 mutation in a family segregating autososomal recessive hypomatuation AI.
the identification of the first active site mutation in MMP20 and provides additional evidence for genetic heterogeneity of the AI.
the molecular genetic analysis of MMP20 in a Turkish family.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MMP20 mutation p.H226Q causes hypomaturation AI in a Turkish family.
the MMP20 gene mutation is responsible for hypomaturation AI in the family in which we identified a novel mutation in the MMP20 gene.
MMP20 gene mutations are rare in Turkish families with autosomal recessively inherited hypomaturation AI, whereas KLK4 gene is not mutated in these families.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mutation of the MMP20 gene causes hypomaturation AI in Turkish patients.
we found a novel missense mutation in the MMP20 gene in the Turkish population with hypomaturation AI and this mutation was found to be the cause of the disease.
MMP20 is the second gene in which mutations have been found in hypomaturation AI, and the p.H226Q mutation is the first MMP20 active site mutation reported to date.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MMP20 gene should be screened in patients with autosomal recessively inherited hypomaturation AI.
the MMP20 gene should be considered in the molecular genetic diagnosis of hypomaturation Amelogenes Imperfecta (HAI).
the MMP20 active site mutation (p.H226R) is a novel cause of autosomal recessive AI.
